# Spoken-conversation filler / register stopword list
#
# Purpose: extend quanteda's built-in English stopword list to catch the
# discourse-marker / backchannel / hedge vocabulary that surfaces as
# filler topics in the K=75 LDA fit on this corpus (T57: "going, know,
# right, got"; T46: profanity-dominated). These words carry near-zero
# THEMATIC content in podcast speech but are frequent enough to form their
# own topics once real content words are diluted around them.
#
# Auditability: every line is one token. Comments (#) and blank lines are
# ignored by r/preprocess.R. Edit by hand; do not generate this
# programmatically, so additions/removals are reviewable in diffs.
#
# BORDERLINE WORDS FLAGGED FOR REVIEW (kept in the list, but each can carry
# real political content in *some* contexts -- see per-word note). If the
# aggressive regime turns out to gut political vocabulary, these are the
# first candidates to drop back out:
#   - right       -- filler ("right?") AND "the right" (political side).
#                    nlp/config.py deliberately left this OUT of the
#                    original FILLER_WORDS for the same reason. Included
#                    here only because it is the single largest driver of
#                    T57; flagged, not silently assumed safe.
#   - left        -- NOT included below (too politically loaded to risk).
#   - like        -- filler AND a real verb ("I like this bill"). Already
#                    in nlp/config.py FILLER_WORDS at 93-98% DF; kept here
#                    too for the R-side list to be self-contained.
#   - well        -- discourse marker AND adverb; low risk, included.
#   - just        -- near-universal hedge; low political content, included.
#   - mean        -- "I mean" filler AND "what does X mean" AND "means"
#                    (methods). Included as filler sense only; DF-based
#                    pruning is the real backstop here, same rationale as
#                    nlp/config.py's note on "mean"/"think".
#
# ---- core spoken-conversation fillers (task spec, verbatim) ----
know
gonna
wanna
gotta
kinda
sorta
yeah
yep
nope
uh
um
hmm
like
mean
right
got
get
go
going
said
say
thing
things
stuff
lot
really
actually
basically
literally
okay
ok
well
just
kind
sort
guy
guys
folks
